Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) are a type of Treasury bond that is indexed to an inflationary gauge to protect investors from a decline in the purchasing power of their money. Since you wouldn’t be alone if you did, the U.S. Treasury created Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) in 1997—special government bonds designed to help protect investors when prices rise across the economy. When inflation rises, both the principal amount you invested and the interest payments you receive increase to help maintain your purchasing power. TIPS spread is the difference in the yields between U.S. treasury bonds and Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities (TIPS) and is a useful measure of the market’s expectation of future Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation. The TIPS spread compares the yield of the TIPS and the yield of regular U.S. Treasury securities with the same maturity dates. This variability of the principal is key as it is linked to the metric, CPI, that measures the level of inflation in the economy. results.snippet: # 10-Year Treasury Bond Yield: What It Is and Why It Matters. These rates indicate the confidence of investors in the economy. The 10-year Treasury note yield is commonly used as a measure of the U.S. government’s 10-year borrowing rate. It serves as a benchmark for other interest rates and is a key indicator of investor sentiment about economic conditions. It matters because it influences borrowing costs of products like mortgages, impacts the valuation of financial assets, and signals expectations about inflation and economic growth. ## Understanding 10-Year Treasury Bond Yields.
